After a dense wave of real estate expansion in the South Bay in 2025, Apple is once again extending its footprint in San Jose. Here are the details.

Apple continues to expand its presence

According to the Mercury News (republished by AppleInsider), Apple has agreed to lease a 125,800-square-foot office building at 580 North Mary Avenue in San Jose.

This deal marks Apple's first major real estate move in the area in 2026. Prior to this, the company spent more than US$1 billion in 2025 to expand its footprint in the South Bay.

The expansion included the US$166.9 million purchase of the three-building Cupertino Gateway complex, the US$350 million acquisition of the two-building Mathilda Commons campus in San Jose, and the US$365 million purchase of the adjacent four-building Mathilda Campus.

Apple subsequently spent another US$216 million to acquire two buildings on Stevens Creek Boulevard in Cupertino, bringing its 2025 Bay Area expansion to more than 1.5 million square feet of office and lab space in total.

Turning back to Apple's new lease, the Mercury News noted that the deal comes as office leasing activity in the South Bay has begun to pick up, with vacancy rates improving both quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year:

Colliers reported that the South Bay office vacancy rate stood at 14.1% in the second quarter of 2026. Colliers defines the market area as Santa Clara County and Fremont.

The report also mentioned that, apart from Apple, Amazon has agreed to lease 316,600 square feet of office space at 1000 Enterprise Road in San Jose.
